proof_audit: Brownian increments are independent of the named filtration, with explicit normal mean/variance; Brownian existence and the usual augmentation theorem are explicitly invoked, not proven by a simulation.

Quadratic variation proved in L2 for deterministic shrinking partitions using Var Q=2 sum h_i²; almost-sure convergence established for dyadic grids with Chebyshev/Borel-Cantelli. Finite total variation contradiction uses that probability-one pathwise dyadic set. No claim for every path-dependent partition.

Elementary Ito isometry and martingale conditional timing are proved with bounded coefficients; truncation/completion extend unbounded L2 cases. Predictable-L2 density proved via generator indicators, clipping, finite maxima and finite-measure countable-union convergence. L2 equality classes and predictable versions are explicit.

Continuous integral version proved using a finite-time first-crossing proof of Doob L2 maximal inequality followed by uniform subsequence convergence; stopped integral compatibility justified by dyadic approximation and isometry. Local zero-drift processes are not silently assigned global zero expectations.

Scalar C1,2 Ito formula proved for continuous adapted coefficients: frozen diffusion remainder controlled by the isometry, squared finite variation/cross terms by Cauchy-Schwarz, weighted Brownian square errors by martingale orthogonality, and time/spatial Taylor remainders by uniform continuity and tight quadratic sums. Rational-time extension makes the identity simultaneous.

Localization explicitly allows one stopped-coefficient jump and immediate stops for unbounded initial random coefficients; zero-time coefficients can be set to zero without altering integrals. Open-state domains and t<T smoothness are stated. General predictable-coefficient/semimartingale Ito is not claimed proved.
Product/cross variation obtained by polarization with a shared Brownian driver. Portfolio value identity is distinguished from the extra self-financing gains condition.

GBM exponential directly verified before applying log; inverse integrating factor proves uniqueness for any continuous competing solution without assuming positivity. Zero initial price and zero volatility handled separately. Gaussian MGF derives real moments, conditional moments and finite-horizon supremum bound.

Euler coupled cross moment derived via the normal MGF derivative, with bias versus MSE units separated. Finite path/cubature, Gaussian analytical expectations and polygon interpolation are explicitly different objects.
